scope: 05-final-project/incident-response/ (responder, evidence collection, autonomy policy, runbooks, incident records)

tools.name: semgrep 1.180.0
tools.config: p/python p/javascript p/typescript p/react p/dockerfile p/github-actions p/secrets (run-semgrep.sh); 150 files, including the 51 new ones

tools.name: pip-audit 2.10.1
tools.config: backend runtime deps from uv.lock (backend-requirements.txt), now 41 packages with the OpenTelemetry SDK and exporter

tools.name: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code)
tools.config: read observability/, incident-response/, the incident records and the responder's agent command; questions: what can the responder read, change and leak, and who can reach it

tools.name: claude -p probes (claude-haiku-5-5)
tools.config: three headless runs with the responder's tool set, each asked to read a file it must not: /etc/hostname (outside the repo), an in-repo file under a deny rule, and backend/.env.example under the final deny list

findings.title: certifi 2026.8.x trusts compromised emSign intermediate CAs
locations: backend/uv.lock (certifi, pulled in by the OTLP exporter via requests)
findings.evidence: The CI security-scan job failed on the first push of the observability branch. certifi is only used by requests inside the OTLP HTTP exporter, which talks plain HTTP to the collector on the Docker network, so no TLS connection relied on the bad roots.
findings.rationale: Not exploitable here, but the upgrade is trivial and a red security-scan job blocks everything else.
findings.fix: certifi 2026.10.19 (commit 76da157, PR #24). pip-audit in this run: 41 packages, 0 known vulnerabilities.

findings.title: Visitors' IP addresses reached the incident record, which is committed to a public repo
findings.evidence: The first test run of the responder copied an internet scanner's IP from the container's access log into evidence/container.log and into the model's summary. Incident folders are committed and the repository is public.
findings.rationale: Personal data in a public repo, and once committed it is in history for good. Redacting before the model sees the evidence also keeps it out of the model's own text.
findings.fix: collect-evidence.sh replaces every public IPv4 address with <public-ip> in every evidence file before the agent runs; private and loopback addresses stay. That test incident was deleted. Both committed incidents contain only 127.0.0.1 and private addresses (checked with a grep for dotted quads).

findings.title: The responder's agent reads attacker-controlled text and its answer is published
findings.evidence: Request paths in container.log come from anyone on the internet, and the agent's summary is committed to a public repo. A prompt injection that made the agent Read a secret and quote it would publish it. Probes with the responder's tool set: headless claude denied a Read of /etc/hostname (outside the repo); a --disallowedTools Read() rule denied an in-repo file; the final deny list denied backend/.env.example and allowed README.md. No real .env file exists inside the repo checkout on the server; prod.env and staging.env are in /srv/card-catalog with mode 600.
findings.rationale: Headless mode already refuses reads outside the working directory, but that depends on the user's Claude Code settings. An explicit deny list holds even if those settings are loosened, and covers a secrets file that someone might one day put inside the repo.
findings.fix: run_agent passes --permission-mode default and --disallowedTools with Read() deny rules for /srv, ~/.claude, ~/.config, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/setup, every .env/.env.*/prod.env/staging.env and *.db. The agent has no Bash, Edit, Write or network tool, and its output is only a schema-checked proposal: policy.py decides, so an injection can at most cause one unneeded staging rollback per hour, or a prod proposal that waits for a human.

findings.title: Grafana uses admin/admin, and the evidence collector logs in with it
findings.evidence: Grafana is published on 127.0.0.1:3000 only (compose.yaml) and is reached through an SSH tunnel. Anyone who can reach it already has a shell on the host.
findings.rationale: The stack runs only for short periods on a resized host. GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD and GRAFANA_AUTH override both defaults if Grafana is ever exposed or kept running.

findings.title: The responder's webhook listens on all interfaces, port 8001
findings.evidence: Grafana reaches it through host.docker.internal from a Docker bridge network, so it can't bind to loopback only. The handler answers 403 to any client that isn't a private or loopback address, before reading the body, and caps the body at 1 MB. A forged alert from inside the host would still only start the same evidence → proposal → policy pipeline. The EC2 security group was not checked in this run (the instance metadata query was refused by the agent's auto mode).
findings.rationale: Code-enforced client check; TCP source addresses can't be usefully spoofed over the internet; the worst case is a policy-bounded staging rollback.

findings.title: deploy.sh deploys any image, including one built locally that never passed CI
findings.evidence: The game day deployed a locally built image (df9cbe0) to staging. Its bug is caught by the unit suite (test_move_position_past_end_appends), but nothing on the server checks that an image came from the CI-gated build. The deploy smoke test passed because it never moves a card. Running deploy.sh needs a shell on the host, so this is a gap in defence in depth, not an exposure.
findings.rationale: Owner approved the fix on 2026-10-22. The gate is defence in depth: running deploy.sh already needs a shell on the host.
findings.fix: deploy.sh verifies every image before deploying: ghcr.io/spycebot/card-catalog:<full sha>, pullable from the registry (local builds refused), and labelled org.opencontainers.image.revision=<that sha>. ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_IMAGE=1 allows a local image onto staging only, for game days. Staging deploys also run backend/scripts/smoke_write.py in the new container (create, move past the end of two columns, delete), which fails on the game-day build (HTTP 500) and passes on main; tests/test_smoke_write.py covers it. Tested on the host: verify refused df9cbe0, card-catalog:local, :main and a foreign registry, and accepted 492ca2a.
